newsitem.title: USA: PIONEER SEES 66 MLN SHARES OUSTANDING AFTER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: PIONEER SEES 66 MLN SHARES OUSTANDING AFTER DEAL.

text.p: Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc said Thursday it expects its shares outstanding will drop to about 66 million from 82 million currently as a result of DuPont Co's $1.7 billion investment in the firm.
DuPont will hold a 20 percent equity and voting rights stake in Pioneer. That stake will be comprised of 16 million shares of a new class of Pioneer stock.

Pioneer officials said the seed and agricultural biotechnology company also plans a self-tender to buy back about 16 million of its shares from the public. That self tender will be held after the DuPont investment is completed.
"The timing will be subject to regulatory approval, a process we are now in," Jerry Chicoine, chief financial officer for Pioneer, told a conference call.
He added it could take two to three months to complete regulatory approval, including Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust review.

In addition to taking a 20 percent stake in Pioneer, DuPont also formed a research alliance and separate joint venture company. The focus of that venture, Pioneer and DuPont officials said, will be to develop grains with improved qualities including oil, protein and carbohydrate content.
Officials said the venture could have over $100 million in sales in 1998 and $3.5 billion in sales within a decade.
